sourcedFrom: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: Dead Air's book for the Wolverine PBS-1 keeps the owner's work on the outside of the can: the thread adapter it mounts by, the Collar, Spring and Lock Ring that lock it to the front sight post pin, the threads, and the exterior finish. The body is a welded structure, and the book says no cleaning of the inside is required — nothing here asks you to open it.

steps.title: Unloaded, magazine out — never on a closed action
steps.action: Before the suppressor is handled, check the chamber and make certain the rifle is unloaded with the magazine removed. If there is any doubt about how, the clearing procedure is in your rifle's own operator's manual, and Dead Air rules out fitting the suppressor to a rifle with a closed action.
steps.prose: The Wolverine goes on many different Kalashnikov variants and their clearing drills differ; only the host's book has yours. An open action is how you see the chamber is empty while your hands are at the muzzle.
steps.quote: CHECK YOUR WEAPON’S CHAMBER AND MAKE CERTAIN THAT THE WEAPON IS UNLOADED AND THE MAGAZINE REMOVED BEFORE PROCEEDING ANY FURTHER.
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 2. PREPARATION, printed p.9
steps.warn: DO NOT INSTALL YOUR NEW SUPPRESSOR ON A FIREARM WITH A CLOSED ACTION!

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: Dead Air's removal procedure opens with a caution that the suppressor may be very hot. Wait until it is cold before you grip the Lock Ring or the Collar — both sit right at the hot end of the barrel.
steps.prose: A can holds heat long after the last shot. Hot threads also bind, which is the moment people reach for force they should not use.
steps.quote: CAUTION: SUPPRESSOR MAY BE VERY HOT!
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 5. REMOVAL FROM HOST FIREARM, printed p.14

steps.title: Lock Ring back until the threads show
steps.action: With the rifle unloaded and pointed in a safe direction, loosen the Lock Ring until the threads on the suppressor body are visible behind it. That frees the Collar to travel.
steps.prose: Until the Lock Ring is backed off, the Collar is clamped onto the front sight post pin and the suppressor cannot turn. Do not try to unscrew the can against it.
steps.quote: Loosen Lock Ring until threads are visible behind it.
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 5. REMOVAL FROM HOST FIREARM, printed p.14
steps.warn: BE CAREFUL NOT TO PINCH YOURSELF ON A LOCK RING THAT HAS NOT BEEN THREADED FULLY FORWARD!

steps.title: Collar off the pin, into position 2 or 3
steps.action: Pull the Collar forward against its Spring so it lifts off the front sight post pin, and rotate it into position 2 (neutral, for turning by hand) or position 3 (fully forward, exposing the wrench flats). The dimple machined into the Collar's knurling shows where its internal lugs sit.
steps.prose: Position 3 is the point of maximum spring load, so it takes some force to get there. Do not stop the Collar where both dimples line up — that is the removal gap, where the Collar comes loose from the body.
steps.quote: Pull Collar forward from front sight post pin and rotate into either position #2 or #3.
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 5. REMOVAL FROM HOST FIREARM, printed p.14

steps.title: Unscrew it — the same way it went on
steps.action: If a wrench was used to torque the suppressor on, set the Collar to position 3 and use the same wrench to take it off. If it went on hand tight, position 2 is enough: grip the knurled body and unscrew it. The standard 14mm Thread Adapter is a left-hand thread, so it unscrews the opposite way to an ordinary thread.
steps.prose: Know your barrel's thread before you put force on it. Turning a left-hand thread the usual way only tightens it, and a can that will not move is telling you that.
steps.quote: Set to Position #3 if a wrench was used to torque suppressor onto the barrel. Use the same wrench to remove.
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 5. REMOVAL FROM HOST FIREARM, printed p.14

steps.title: Field strip complete — off the host
steps.action: With the suppressor off the rifle, the routine service is all Dead Air asks for: keep the threads clean and wipe the outside with good quality gun oil. The welded body is not opened, and the book says no cleaning of the inside is required.
steps.prose: The Collar and the Thread Adapter come off only to fit the can to a different host, and that is not a cleaning job.
steps.quote: No cleaning of the inside of the suppressor is required.
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 7. DISASSEMBLY & CLEANING, printed p.17

steps.title: Clean threads, oiled outside
steps.action: Clean the threads — the suppressor's adapter and the rifle's muzzle — and wipe down the outside of the can with good quality gun oil. That is the whole of the maintenance the book describes.
steps.prose: Carbon on the threads is what stops the adapter coming to rest square on the muzzle face, and a can that does not seat square loses its alignment with the bore.
steps.quote: Typically there is very little maintenance needed with respect to your suppressor other than to keep the threads clean and to wipe down the outside with good quality gun oil.
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 7. DISASSEMBLY & CLEANING, printed p.17

steps.title: Test any solvent on a small spot first
steps.action: The outside carries a Nitride and Cerakote finish. Before a solvent goes on the whole can, try it on a small area and see what it does to the finish.
steps.prose: The finish is very durable, but Dead Air singles out solvents as the thing to be careful with. Gun oil on a cloth is the book's cleaner.
steps.quote: Always test a small area before applying a solvent to the suppressor as a whole.
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 7. DISASSEMBLY & CLEANING, printed p.17

steps.title: Check bore alignment before you shoot it
steps.action: Kalashnikov barrels vary a great deal in thread quality and muzzle alignment. Use the Wolverine only on a rifle with good threads and muzzle alignment, and check that the bore lines up with the suppressor before shooting it, even though the can is built with a very liberal bore.
steps.prose: A muzzle thread that is not true to the bore points the suppressor off the bullet's path, and that is what a strike comes from.
steps.quote: While the suppressor is designed with a very liberal bore, it is important to check bore alignment with the suppressor prior to shooting.
steps.cite: WOLVERINE PBS-1 — Rev121323 — 2. PREPARATION, printed p.9

deepAbsentReason: Dead Air publishes no deeper cleaning for the Wolverine PBS-1. Its Disassembly & Cleaning section (printed p.17) asks only for clean threads and an oiled exterior and states that no cleaning of the inside of the suppressor is required, and the book describes the body as a complete welded structure (printed p.10). The only parts-off procedures in it — Collar removal and Thread Adapter replacement (printed pp.10–11, 15–16) — are for fitting the can to a different host, using a Wolverine-specific collet wrench and a torque wrench, not for cleaning.

cleaning.name: THREADS
tasks: Keep the suppressor's adapter threads clean
The rifle's muzzle threads clean and lubed before the suppressor goes back on
The metric adapter seats on the barrel's muzzle face, not on a shoulder — keep that face clean
Do not thread it onto a barrel whose muzzle face is not cut square to the bore

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR FINISH
tasks: Wipe down the outside with good quality gun oil
Nitride and Cerakote finish: test any solvent on a small area first

cleaning.name: COLLAR, SPRING & LOCK RING
tasks: A light amount of lube on the cam surface, threads and lugs keeps the Collar moving smoothly
The Spring stays fully seated in its groove on the Thread Adapter

cleaning.name: INSIDE THE CAN
tasks: ⛔ Nothing inside — Dead Air says no cleaning of the inside of the suppressor is required
Do not open the welded body

reassembly: Rifle unloaded and pointed in a safe direction, and its muzzle threads clean and lubed.
Set the Collar to position 2 or 3 so its notches will not hit the front sight post pin while you tighten.

Thread the suppressor onto the barrel carefully, without cross threading or forcing it — the standard 14mm Thread Adapter is left-hand threaded and comes to rest on the muzzle face, with some threads still showing when it is fully tight. If it does not thread on smoothly, stop and contact Dead Air's Customer Service Department.

Tighten it all the way against the barrel: by hand on the knurled body with the Collar in position 2, or a light torque with a wrench with the Collar in position 3. Do not over tighten. On the 24mm adapter, use only the small flats on a barrel, at less than 15 ft-lbs.

With the Lock Ring fully loosened, compress the Collar and rotate it back to position 1 so its teeth engage the front sight post pin. If no notch falls on the pin, rotate the Collar slightly either way until the closest one does.
Make sure the Collar is not sitting at the removal gap (both dimples aligned) — there it is loose, rests against the front sight post, and a tightened Lock Ring pushes the can toward unscrewing.
Grasp the Collar firmly and tighten the Lock Ring against it as forcefully as you can.
fncheck: Rifle unloaded and the can cold: the suppressor is tight against the barrel, the Collar sits in position 1 with a notch on the front sight post pin, and the Lock Ring is tightened hard against it. Dead Air recommends checking tightness and engagement periodically, because all direct thread suppressors may loosen with use. If it will not thread on smoothly, stop and contact Dead Air's Customer Service Department.
